newsitem.title: UK: London stocks hit record, Nikkei edges lower.
newsitem.headline: London stocks hit record, Nikkei edges lower.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Spurred by a strong lead from Wall Street and renewed takeover speculation, the FTSE 100 pushed further into uncharted territory to close at a record. The benchmark blue chip index settled 24.7 points higher at 4,115.7.

FRANKFURT - Germany's 30-share DAX index of blue-chip shares closed the last day's trade of the year at a day's high as the bull market continued to prevail and the stronger dollar lifted shares. The index came off a little as the session went on, but rallied towards the end to close at 2,888.69 points, up 35.81 points. This closing price represents an increase of 28.16 percent on the closing price on the last day in 1995.

PARIS - French stocks finished higher, underpinned by gains on Wall Street and leading European bourses, brokers said. Block trades ahead of Tuesday's expiry of futures and options accounted for much of the activity. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 11.68 points at 2,318.63.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended at a record close after a day of quiet trade that was characterised by position-squaring and window dressing ahead of the year-end. Trading on Tuesday is expected to be even quieter and the Swiss Exchange will close early at 1300 GMT. The broad SPI ended 14.54 points higher at 2,515.62, a record close.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's benchmark Nikkei 225 index ended the final session of 1996 little changed, after recouping early losses brought on by the yen's weakening against the dollar and fears that trade related to margin expiry would weigh down the index, brokers said. The Nikkei 225 ended 7.69 points lower at 19,361.35.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended higher on buying in finance counters and an easing of futures-related selling in the afternoon. The Hang Seng Index jumped 76.61 points to close at 13,480.75 after trading to a high of 13,503.18.

SYDNEY - A thinly traded Australian share market climbed to a record close with a combination of end-of-year window-dressing and futures-led trading providing most of the impetus. The All Ordinaries index added 17.3 points to 2,412.9 after reaching a record intraday high of 2,416.8.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended the last full trading day of 1996 in a buoyant mood as the industrial index surged ahead. Record closes in New York on Friday and London on Monday provided powerful impetus for the South African market. The all-share index rose 45.4 points to end at 6,628.5 as industrials edged up 71.6 points to finish the day at 7,887.4. The gold index put on 5.4 points to 1,500.7.
